passage:
The school placed a colored flag near the playground to show air quality. Green meant outdoor activities were fine. Yellow meant students with breathing problems should be careful. Red meant outdoor exercise would be limited.
Some students complained on red-flag days because they wanted PE outside. The nurse explained that air can look clear and still contain harmful particles.
The science teacher brought a sensor to class and showed real-time readings. Students were surprised that invisible things could affect health.
The flag became more respected after that.
A warning works better when people understand what it is warning them about. Invisible danger needs visible signals.
